subject: Arclight — Private deployment capability questionnaire
messages:
From: Samantha Boyle <samantha.boyle@arclightsys.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Arclight Systems Security <security@arclightsys.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Arclight — Private deployment capability questionnaire

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call earlier. As promised, attached is our formal capability questionnaire for private/on-prem deployments. We need to confirm a few items so our procurement and infosec teams can complete the security review and move to the pilot (we have an internal timeline targeting a June dry-run). High-level asks:

- Network isolation model: can Redwood support a pure egress-blocked deployment with only a private NTP and CRL distribution feed?
- Operator access: we need details on operator role separation, SSO, and whether HSM-backed keys are required for your KMS integrations.
- Patch & patch validation flow in air-gapped environments (how are signed updates delivered, verified, and rolled back?).
- Offline telemetry and alerting: what minimal metrics are available when the control plane is offline?

I've attached a short spreadsheet (arclight_rfi_template.xlsx) with line items we expect to be answered; please return as a completed sheet. Also attaching our network diagram for reference.

Attachments: arclight_rfi_template.xlsx, arclight_network_diagram.pdf

Appreciate a response by EOD Friday PT so we can keep the review on schedule.

Best,
Samantha Boyle
Senior Technical Program Manager — Arclight Systems
Samantha.Boyle@arclightsys.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Boyle <samantha.boyle@arclightsys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arclight — Private deployment capability questionnaire

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending this over and for the sync earlier. We've started a working thread internally; I'm looping Vanessa (deploy lead) and Karthik (security/ops).

Quick answers up front:
- Network isolation: yes, Redwood Private supports full egress restriction. We can operate with only customer-provided NTP and CRL endpoints. We also support static allowlists for operator workstations in our recommended architecture.
- Operator access: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and can integrate with customer IdPs. For KMS, we support both customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS and HSM-backed appliances) and our managed vault; for air-gapped installs customers commonly bring an HSM appliance (we describe integration below).
- Patching: signed artifacts + detached signatures are used. We provide a verification tool (offline verifier) and a rollback manifest. Patch delivery to air-gapped environments is via offline media, and our ops runbook documents the verification steps.
- Offline telemetry: bundle-based health snapshots and local alerting agents remain available; control-plane telemetry is buffered locally and can be exported via secure media.

I'll attach our operator handoff checklist and a short runbook excerpt — please complete the spreadsheet you sent and return; we'll fill in any gaps.

Attachments: redwood_operator_checklist.xlsx (attached)

Next steps: if you can complete the sheet by Thursday EOD we'll aim to provide the completed answers and a short architecture appendix by Friday.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
loganw@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 (650) 555-0123

From: Samantha Boyle <samantha.boyle@arclightsys.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arclight — Private deployment capability questionnaire

Logan — attached is our completed RFI (arclight_rfi_answers.xlsx). A few clarifications inline below and in the sheet:

- Network: we are strict about no outbound to the internet except to: customer NTP, internal CRL distribution point, and a named ticketing endpoint used only for incident ingestion (all via private peering). Please confirm Redwood's support for static ARP and enforced DNS-over-TLS from the deployed hosts.
- KMS: our security team requires HSM-backed key origin for root signing keys. We can provide an on-prem HSM (Luna or Thales) and expect Redwood to integrate via PKCS#11.
- Patch cadence: monthly security-only updates; for air-gapped we will ship signed tarballs via SFTP through an approved transfer node. Provide the checklist we should follow for signature verification and rollback.

Attachments included: arclight_rfi_answers.xlsx, arclight_network_diagram.pdf, ndas_signed_arclight.pdf

Thanks — let me know if you need us to schedule a technical deep-dive with your ops team next week.

— Samantha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Arclight RFI — follow-ups and HSM confirmation

Folks — reviewed their answers. Two quick items we need to confirm before sending final response:

1) PKCS#11 integration: we support it but need Karthik to confirm whether our packaged runtime includes the necessary middleware or if the customer must install the HSM client. Also need exact supported vendors list (Thales, Luna, Utimaco).
2) DNS-over-TLS: our recommended host image can enforce stub resolvers that negotiate DoT, but their environment's appliance may terminate TLS; clarify the operational implication and document fallback.

Karthik — can you take point on #1 and draft a short note we can include in the architecture appendix? I'll handle #2 and drop a short operations note.

-Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Arclight RFI — follow-ups and HSM confirmation

Taking this. Short answer: we support Thales (nShield/Luna) and Utimaco via PKCS#11; the customer must install the vendor HSM client on the operator jump host or on a dedicated key broker VM that we reference from the runtime. Our packaging includes the PKCS#11 shim and integration tests, but vendor client libs are redistributed under vendor license and typically installed by customer (we provide exact package names and install steps).

I'll draft the compatibility note and the sample systemd restart hooks for the HSM client. Targeting the note by EOD Thursday.

-Karthik

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Boyle <samantha.boyle@arclightsys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Arclight — Private deployment capability questionnaire

Hi Samantha — thanks for the completed sheet and the diagram. Attached are the items we promised and a short architecture appendix addressing your asks. Highlights:

- Network isolation: Confirmed — Redwood Private can be deployed with strict egress controls. We recommend a dedicated transfer node for SFTP media exchange and an outbound allowlist limited to your NTP/CRL/ticketing endpoints. DNS-over-TLS is supported at the host layer; we note a potential termination at the edge and include a fallback configuration.
- HSM/KMS: We support PKCS#11 for Thales (nShield/Luna) and Utimaco. Customer installs the vendor client on the key broker VM; Redwood's runtime talks to the broker over a mTLS channel. Included: sample systemd units and an integration checklist.
- Patching & verification: we provide an offline verifier binary (sha256 + detached signature). Patch rollout steps and rollback manifest included in the operator checklist.
- Offline telemetry: local health bundles + a secure export workflow.

Attachments: redwood_operator_checklist.xlsx (updated), architecture_appendix_arclight.pdf, arclight_integration_compatibility_note.txt

Next steps: 1) Please review the architecture appendix; 2) if acceptable, let's schedule a 90-minute technical run-through with your ops and HSM vendor week of 2026-06-01; 3) we'll open a HubSpot deal stage 'Pilot — Contracting' (HS-2345678) and arrange NDAs/gating as needed (I attached the signed NDA copy you sent).

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cArclightOnprem

If that works I'll have contracting reach out with a statement of work and proposed timeline.

Thanks again — Logan
